cim: Center for Business, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation Hosts Holly Wiggins as Inaugural Speaker
cim_eredeti: Center for Business, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation Hosts Holly Wiggins as Inaugural Speaker
szoveg_eredeti:
On Nov. 16, Sweet Briar’s new Center for Business, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation welcomed its inaugural guest speaker for a discussion on the future of artificial intelligence (AI) and how women should be at the forefront of the field.

Holly Wiggins, an enterprise account director for Asana’s public sector and former USDA chief strategy officer for science and research, presented “The Future is Not Artificial. It’s Ours. Why Women Must Lead the Next Age of Intelligence” to an engaged audience of students, faculty, staff, and guests.

“We’ve spent years asking whether AI will become more human, and I know there’s a lot of ideas about that, but I actually think we’re asking the wrong question. We should be asking, ‘what happens if we become less human?’” Wiggins said during her talk.

During the event, Wiggins touched on other topics at the forefront of discussions on AI happening every day across the country, including how society and those using AI influence what it “knows” and therefore outputs, and how biases can and are transferring. Wiggins explained that AI is a mirror of the inputs it receives, which is why she wants to see women at the forefront of the “next age of intelligence.”

“My philosophy has and always will be collaboration, not competition. AI reflects whoever is in the data and whoever is in the room. Right now, it’s reflecting older systems and older data. It can reflect our past, it can reflect our present, or it can reflect the future that we all want to create. The only way we see ourselves in that mirror is to take part right now, in this great transformation. If we don’t participate, we won’t be reflected,” she said. “Now we’re in an age of new intelligence, one that is both artificial and human, and we need women leaders. We need Sweet Briar alumnae. We need the local community. We need faculty. We need every one of you to stand up and help shape this new age of intelligence and what it becomes.”

Sweet Briar community members attend Holly Wiggins' talk.

Launched this fall, the Center for Business, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation will prepare students for successful careers after graduation and will augment the Sweet Briar’s existing business major and other academic areas across the College through new programming, additional internships, apprenticeships, opportunities to hear guest speakers, and more.

“Holly’s message captures exactly what we hope to accomplish through the new Center for Business, Entrepreneurship, and Innovation,” said Laura Townsend, the center’s director. “We want to empower our students not simply to adapt to a rapidly changing world, but to actively shape its future. By connecting students across all disciplines with visionary leaders, emerging technologies, and real-world opportunities, we hope to inspire them to think boldly, challenge conventional thinking, and recognize their potential to lead meaningful change. Holly’s visit was a wonderful way to launch that vision and begin building a community of innovation and entrepreneurship at Sweet Briar.”

Holly Wiggins is a strategy and innovation executive, keynote speaker, entrepreneur, and advocate for women’s leadership in the age of artificial intelligence. At Asana, she helps organizations navigate the future of work through human-centered AI, agentic technology, and new approaches to collaboration between people and intelligent systems. Her enterprise portfolio spans major U.S. and Canadian government institutions, federal science and research agencies, regulatory bodies, higher education, and leading aerospace and emerging technology organizations. Before joining Asana, Holly spent 18 years in federal government service, including her role at the USDA. Her career spans nearly three decades of experience in strategy, innovation, organizational transformation, and executive leadership. She is also the founder of Ladies Level Up, through which she champions women’s leadership in science, technology, and artificial intelligence through her philosophy of “Collaboration, Not Competition.” She is also co-founder of theCommons Academy, a mission-driven education company focused on preparing people for the future of work. Wiggins holds an M.B.A. from Texas A&M University and a master’s degree in international policy and practice from George Washington University. She studied international human rights law at the University of Oxford, and completed American University’s Key Executive Leadership Program. To learn more or connect with Holly Wiggins, visit hollywiggins.com.
